definition: taking effect from a date in the past
memoryTip: Retro = back: the rule reaches backward in time.
correctPassage: The pay raise was retroactive to January, so employees received months of back pay.
wrongPassages: She preferred retroactive furniture that looked like it came from the 1950s.
The coach ran a retroactive drill so the team could practice the play again.
His retroactive mood made him refuse every new idea on principle.

definition: respond to a gesture or action with a corresponding one
memoryTip: Reciprocal: give back the same kind of gesture you got.
correctPassage: When one nation cut tariffs, trading partners were expected to reciprocate.
wrongPassages: He tried to reciprocate the broken vase by gluing the shards back together.
The engine will reciprocate fuel into electricity more efficiently this year.
She hoped to reciprocate her essay by cutting it from five pages to two.

memoryTip: Dis + engage: unhook yourself and step away.
correctPassage: Mediators urged both armies to disengage and pull back from the border.
wrongPassages: The company planned to disengage three new factories next quarter.
She tried to disengage the audience by telling a long, lively story.
Judges will disengage the winner after scoring each routine.

definition: causing or likely to cause argument; quarrelsome
memoryTip: Full of contention — built to start a fight.
correctPassage: Land rights remain a contentious issue that splits the community.
wrongPassages: The museum display was contentious, packing a thousand years into one case.
Her contentious notes summarized every lecture in neat bullet points.
They chose a contentious hotel because it was quiet and inexpensive.

definition: open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous
memoryTip: Equi-vocal: equal voices, so the meaning cuts both ways.
correctPassage: His answer was deliberately equivocal, satisfying neither side completely.
wrongPassages: The coach was equivocal about practice, repeating the same drills every day.
She gave an equivocal speech praising the team without a single reservation.
The recipe was equivocal, listing exact grams for every ingredient.

definition: not clearly visible or attracting attention
memoryTip: In-conspicuous: the opposite of flashy — easy to miss.
correctPassage: The security camera is small enough to stay inconspicuous in the hallway.
wrongPassages: Her inconspicuous costume, covered in sequins, lit up the whole stage.
The billboard was inconspicuous, towering over the highway in neon.
He made an inconspicuous entrance by arriving with a marching band.

definition: combine two things into one, often mistakenly
memoryTip: Con-flate: fuse two ideas into one (sometimes wrongly).
correctPassage: Critics warned not to conflate correlation with causation in the study.
wrongPassages: Engineers will conflate the bridge by replacing every rusted bolt.
She tried to conflate the argument by calmly listing each side’s points.
The bank will conflate the loan so borrowers have more time to repay.

definition: build or form again from parts; restore
memoryTip: Re-constitute: put the pieces back together as a whole.
correctPassage: Add warm water to reconstitute the powdered soup before serving.
wrongPassages: The mayor vowed to reconstitute traffic by adding more stop signs downtown.
She will reconstitute the novel by cutting the final three chapters.
Judges reconstitute scores so the lowest mark automatically wins.

definition: lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern
memoryTip: A-pathos: no feeling — you simply don’t care.
correctPassage: Voter apathy, not anger, explained the record-low turnout.
wrongPassages: Her apathy for the project showed in late nights and extra revisions.
The crowd’s apathy exploded into cheers when the underdog scored.
Doctors treated his apathy with ice packs and a compression bandage.

definition: unchanging over time; unable to be altered
memoryTip: Im-mutable: cannot mutate — locked in place forever.
correctPassage: In the model, physical constants are treated as immutable.
wrongPassages: Fashion is immutable, flipping styles every few seasons.
His immutable mood swung from joy to rage within an hour.
They kept an immutable schedule so meetings could move as needed.
